name: The Test of Righteousness
summary: At Jordan Stilwell’s forge outside Ironforge, a paladin awaits the making of a mighty warhammer. You have gathered perilous components across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor for the smith. The hammer marks an apprentice’s passage into a recognized champion of the Light.

sections.title: A Smith's Tribute
sections.body: Outside Ironforge’s gates, master smith Jordan Stilwell works at his forge. He admits to envying paladins who wander the land, yet takes pride in serving their cause with hammer and anvil. You bring him rare materials gathered from shadowy crypts, sunken ruins, and dangerous mines. With them, Stilwell keeps his promise and forges a weapon worthy of a true defender.

sections.title: The Legacy of Bosch Verigan
sections.body: Jordan Stilwell names the finished warhammer Verigan's Fist, honoring Bosch Verigan, an honored dwarven paladin and his dear friend. On behalf of himself and his wife, he places the sacred weapon in a young champion's hands. Through it, the memory and valor of his fallen friend endure against the darkness threatening Azeroth.

faq.q: What happens during this step of the quest?
faq.answer: Jordan Stilwell works the components you gathered at his anvil, striking hot metal in his forge. When the work is done, he presents you with the finished weapon.
Bosch Verigan was an honored dwarven paladin and a close friend of Jordan Stilwell. Jordan named the newly forged two-handed hammer for him, honoring his devotion to the Holy Light.

faq.q: Where does this forging take place?
faq.answer: Jordan Stilwell forges the hammer just outside Ironforge’s great gates in the snowy peaks of Dun Morogh, where he keeps his forge and anvil.

faq.q: Why did Jordan need rare materials from all over the world?
faq.answer: Jordan Stilwell needed rare materials from perilous places across the world to forge a weapon of exceptional balance and holy resonance. The ores, wood, and gemstones were needed to make a hammer that could endure a paladin's sacred wrath.

faq.q: Does Jordan Stilwell ever fight in battle himself?
faq.answer: Jordan Stilwell is a blacksmith, not a wandering warrior. He admits to envying those who roam the land, but finds pride and purpose in crafting weapons for defenders of the Light.

faq.q: What does receiving this hammer signify for a paladin?
faq.answer: Receiving the hammer marks the end of a paladin's long trials. It shows the bearer has the courage, persistence, and holy conviction to champion the Light in Azeroth's most dangerous corners.

angles.text: As a paladin, your perilous journeys across distant lands earn you Verigan's Fist, a weapon devoted to upholding righteousness.
As a blacksmith, you can see how Jordan Stilwell's masterful work gives raw steel and salvaged materials a holy purpose.
As a dwarf, you carry a hammer forged to preserve the memory of Bosch Verigan, an honored dwarven paladin who embodied the resilience of Khaz Modan.
